rows.verified: COSHH requires adequate control of exposure to workplace substances that can cause ill health.
Hazardous substances may include chemicals, fumes, dusts, vapours, mists, gases and biological agents.
Employers must assess risks arising from use, storage, handling and disposal of hazardous substances.
Exposure should be prevented or, where prevention is not reasonably practicable, adequately controlled.
Reducing emission, release and spread at source is a core principle of good control practice.
Control measures may include enclosure, local exhaust ventilation, procedures, supervision and training.
Control measures should be maintained, examined and tested where required so they remain effective.
Workers need information, instruction and training on hazards, precautions and emergency arrangements.
The correct controls depend on the substance, route of exposure, concentration, process, duration and affected workers.
COSHH evidence is substance- and process-specific and is not an exact parcel-level probability.
Failure of pressure equipment can cause serious injury, fatalities and major property damage.
Users must provide pressure equipment that is safe, suitable for its intended purpose and correctly installed.
Safe operating limits and the characteristics of the relevant fluid must be known.
Suitable protective devices such as safety valves or bursting discs must be fitted where required.
Protective devices must be correctly set and maintained in effective working order.
Pressure systems need suitable maintenance that considers age, use and operating environment.
A written scheme of examination is required for qualifying pressure systems before operation where the regulations apply.
Examinations must be carried out by a competent person in accordance with the written scheme.
Whether the pressure-system regulations apply depends on the equipment, relevant fluid, pressure and specific exclusions.
Pressure-system evidence is equipment- and operating-condition-specific and is not an exact parcel-level probability.
